summary: AWS Marketplace purchase completed but entitlement not active in Redwood (activation delay >2 hours)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer purchased Redwood Inference via AWS Marketplace and expected immediate entitlement activation, but Redwood Console continued to show "No marketplace entitlement detected" and API requests returned "payment_required" for the org.

Customer impact:
- Buyer cannot proceed with onboarding (org linking blocked).
- Procurement is time-sensitive: customer is trying to align spend to AWS commit and needs confirmation the subscription is active.
- Customer reports purchase completed in AWS Marketplace around 09:08 PT; entitlement not reflected in Redwood as of 11:20 PT.

Customer-reported details:
- AWS Marketplace subscription: Active (customer shared screenshot)
- AWS account: customer did not share account ID in ticket; provided Marketplace "Entitlement ID" prefix only (redacted here)
- Intended Redwood org: "northwind-prod"
- Purchase SKU: "Redwood Inference - Hosted API (Enterprise)" (customer terminology; may map to Hosted API + support add-on)

Environment:
- Redwood: prod, us-east
- Marketplace integration path: AWS entitlement events -> webhook ingestion -> entitlement mapping -> org entitlements

Repro steps (support):
1) Customer purchases via AWS Marketplace.
2) Customer signs into Redwood Console and attempts to link AWS Marketplace subscription.
3) Console shows entitlement pending/not found.
4) Any API calls billed under org return payment/entitlement errors.

Initial triage notes:
- This appears to be delayed ingestion/processing rather than a missing purchase.
- Similar symptoms observed intermittently during marketplace refresh staging tests (see #eng thread 1739153300) but not expected in prod.

Requested from customer (sent 2026-01-14):
- AWS payer account ID (12 digits)
- AWS Marketplace product code and customer identifier if available
- Approx purchase timestamp (UTC) and subscription ID

Internal investigation (high level):
- Verified Marketplace ingestion service is up.
- Observed increased lag on entitlement processing worker queue in us-east.
- Identified parsing/validation issue on select entitlement events where the effective timestamp is interpreted incorrectly, causing event to be deferred.

Resolution summary:
- Support performed a one-time manual entitlement backfill for the customer subscription to unblock onboarding.
- Engineering deployed hotfix to correct timestamp handling and prevent deferred processing.
- Added alerting threshold for marketplace entitlement lag to catch recurrence sooner.

internal_notes:
Key technical signals:
- Webhook ingress healthy (2xx), but entitlement activation lag spiked.
- Worker queue depth increased; events were not failing, they were being deferred.
- Root cause identified: effectiveDate parsing/validation bug causing some AWS entitlement payloads to be treated as future-dated, preventing immediate activation.

Relevant logs (redacted):
- marketplace-entitlements-worker (us-east):
  2026-01-14T19:11:32.118Z level=INFO msg="received entitlement event" provider=aws req_id=01H... customer_id=aws-cust-... product_code=redwood-... effective_date="2026-01-14T17:08:00Z"
  2026-01-14T19:11:32.121Z level=WARN msg="deferring entitlement activation" reason="effectiveDate_in_future" parsed_effective_date="2026-01-14T17:08:00-0800" now="2026-01-14T19:11:32Z" defer_for_seconds=28800 entitlement_event_id=ent-...

Actions taken:
- Manual entitlement attach to unblock customer (documented in marketplace-provisioning-and-troubleshooting-guide under "Entitlement backfill").
- Hotfix PR: redwood/pr-18522 (timestamp handling + remove incorrect deferral).
- SRE to add/verify alerts: marketplace_entitlement_lag_seconds p95 > 600s (us-east) and deferred_entitlement_events > 0 sustained 10m.

Security/compliance:
- No indication of unauthorized access; this is a processing/timing issue.
- Avoid requesting screenshots that include AWS account IDs unless needed; use subscription ID + payer account in secure channel when required.
resolution:
Resolved via manual entitlement backfill for affected customer subscription + product hotfix deployed to production to prevent recurrence.

Customer-facing resolution:
- Entitlement activated and detected in Console; customer successfully linked AWS Marketplace subscription to Redwood org and proceeded with onboarding.

Engineering resolution:
- Deployed redwood/pr-18522 to correct AWS entitlement effectiveDate handling.
- Reduced entitlement processing lag back to normal operating range in us-east.

Follow-ups:
- Confirm dashboards/alerts added for entitlement lag and deferred event count (ENG-4407).
- Add runbook step for quickly identifying deferred entitlement events by payer account/subscription ID.
